transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-29
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE); Maya Lopez (AtlasHealth Head of ML), Samir Patel (DevOps Lead), Jordan Reed (CTO), Avery Kim (Product PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Walkthrough of Console usage heatmap, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown; focus on reducing inference spend for chat endpoints and embeddings used for clinical search.
- Discussed tradeoffs: hosted vs Dedicated (predictable throughput), caching strategies, and route-level tagging for billing.
- Agreed next steps: pricing spreadsheet, sandbox perf run, customer to provide anonymized sample traffic.

Topics: usage-heatmap, per-route-cost, dedicated-vs-hosted, caching, security docs, SSO/SAML, SOC2

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We got Maya, Samir, Jordan and Avery from AtlasHealth, and I think we'll kick off, quick intros and then Priya will jump into the console heatmap.
[00:18] Maya: Hi! Yeah thanks, I saw the invite. We're especially interested in how you can show cost by route — we run a few different AI routes for chat triage, embeddings for search, and a rerank flow.
[00:31] Priya: Great, that's exactly what the route dashboards are for. Quick note, I'm Priya, I'm on the SE team, I'll demo the Console and then Liam will jump into some time-series and the Optimize suggestions.
[00:45] Jordan: Also curious about Dedicated vs hosted. We have regulatory constraints, but cost predictability is a big concern.
[00:53] Alex: Totally. We'll cover Dedicated later. For now, Priya?
[01:02] Priya: Alright opening the Console -> Usage -> Heatmap. So at the top we have overall token volume by hour for the last 30 days, and below that a per-route breakdown. The heatmap lets you spot bursty routes — you can see their chat-triage route spikes at 14:00 and again at 02:00 UTC.
[01:27] Samir: Are those hours local to our org or UTC? The timestamps sound like UTC.
[01:33] Priya: Good call, it's UTC by default, you can change timezone in preferences. Also note the heatmap aggregates both prompt and completion tokens, so high intensity often maps to long generation.
[01:50] Maya: The demo looks nice, but how do we map this to dollar cost? We need to show finance per app feature.
[01:57] Priya: We have per-route cost attribution. Clicking on the route drills down to route metrics: tokens, latency P95, average prompt length, model variant usage and the cost split: compute + model price + infra overhead.
[02:15] Priya: Example - the embeddings route is 34% of your total spend but only 12% of requests, because embeddings are expensive per unit.
[02:26] Avery: That's the exact kind of insight we need. Can we tag routes by product team?
[02:31] Priya: Yes, you can add tags to routes either via the SDK header or Console. Then on the cost view you can group by tag — so finance can get a product-level P&L.
[02:45] [crosstalk] Jordan: And what's the accuracy of the attribution if we have prefix caching, like KV cache?
[02:52] Priya: We account for KV cache hits — the Console shows cache hit-rate and a 'saved tokens' estimate, though the saved cost is an approximation because it depends on your model routing and batch shapes.
[03:08] Alex: Quick interjection — one thing customers ask is how batching affects per-token latency vs cost. We'll show an Optimize suggestion later for batching thresholds.
[03:19] Liam: Jumping into the route drill. Here is the timeline: tokens, calls, model variant used. See this small pie chart for GPU types — important when you're on Dedicated because different GPU families change cost.
[03:33] Samir: On Dedicated, can we pin a node type to specific routes? We want the embeddings route on A100 and the chat on H100.
[03:40] Liam: Yes, with Dedicated you can create pools and route policies to send traffic to a pool. You can pin model variants and kernel-quant configs to pools. There are limits but it's generally available.
[03:55] Maya: Security question — we need SOC 2 and SSO integration, plus customer-managed keys.
[04:02] Alex: We support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption options and SOC 2 compliance. We'll share our security pack.
[04:17] Maya: Great. Also data residency — EU only for some PHI-adjacent datasets.
[04:23] Alex: Private deployment in a VPC or on-prem package covers that. We'll include options in the doc.
[04:33] Priya: Back to cost — here's the cost waterfall view for the selected route. Top line is endpoint spend, then breakdown by model price, GPU hours, autoscaling overhead, and data egress.
[04:48] Priya: Note the autoscale buffer shows as a separate line; if you choose lower minimums and smaller cooldowns the buffer cost goes down but your risk of cold-start increases.
[05:02] Samir: Our main concern is predictable monthly spend, not necessarily absolute minimum. We prefer a commit for budget certainty.
[05:10] Alex: That's where Dedicated comes in — reserved capacity commitments give predictable throughput and unit costs. We'll draft a couple of commit sizing options.
[05:20] Maya: Awesome. Can you show how the console surfaces anomalous spend? We had a surprise spike last month.
[05:28] Priya: Sure, there's an anomalies tab. It flags deviations in tokens, cost-per-route, and sudden model variant shifts. It links back to request samples and the route filter.
[05:39] Priya: Example anomaly: a rerank route had a sudden 5x increase in prompt length due to an upstream change — Console detected it and sent an alert.
[05:49] Jordan: Alerts — can they route to Slack and PagerDuty?
[05:53] Priya: Yes, webhooks to Slack, Microsoft Teams, and PagerDuty integrations available.
[06:01] Avery: The heatmap is helpful. How granular is the cost breakdown? Can we get per-request costing for chargebacks?
[06:08] Liam: You can export per-request logs with token counts and model used, then use a per-token price to compute chargebacks. We also provide a CSV export and a billing API.
[06:19] Samir: If we export logs, are they PII sanitized? We can't export PHI offsite.
[06:25] Alex: For PHI you should use Private deployment. In hosted we keep transcripts encrypted and redaction tools can be applied, but full PHI export off-host is constrained by compliance. We'll mark that as a must-ask.
[06:38] [10-minute mark note: discussion continued on routing and caching]
[10:12] Priya: Now flipping to Optimize -> Suggestions. For your chat-triage route, Optimize recommends prefix caching for repeated system prompts, and lowering max new tokens on confirm step; model suggestion is to try a 8-bit quantized variant for low-latency tasks.
[10:35] Maya: Curious about quality tradeoffs — will quantized models degrade triage accuracy?
[10:40] Priya: It depends on the model. We recommend A/B testing: Redwood can host a canary using the quantized variant for a small percentage of traffic. Console will compare quality metrics against your eval set.
[10:51] Jordan: Eval sets — do you support attaching our own eval prompts?
[10:54] Priya: Yes, you can upload prompt sets and reference outputs; Console calculates BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and custom pass/fail thresholds. Also you can hook into our regression alerts.
[11:08] Samir: For the sandbox perf run, what do you need from us?
[11:12] Priya: A) a sample traffic CSV with route names, timestamped request counts, average prompt length; B) an anchor eval set for each route; C) target SLOs (p50/p95 latency, cost cap).
[11:23] Samir: We'll pull that together.
[11:27] Alex: We'll also provide a suggested batching policy. In many cases slight batching reduces token cost by 20-30% without hurting p95 too much.
[11:38] Maya: Any built-in support for tenant-level billing? We multi-tenant our app and need internal chargebacks.
[11:45] Liam: Yes, you can map routes to tenants via tags and generate tenant-level billing reports. There's also an API to pull per-tenant spend.
[11:55] Maya: Okay. Quick question: our embeddings pipeline is currently on a cloud provider-managed instance — can Redwood route only the embedding calls to Dedicated and keep the rest hosted?
[12:03] Priya: Absolutely. Policy-based routing allows you to send traffic by route name, header, or token. You'll be able to mix Dedicated pools with hosted fallback.
[12:15] Jordan: And if Dedicated pool is saturated, is there automated fallback to a lower-cost hosted model?
[12:21] Liam: Yes, you can configure fallbacks with priority policies — eg fall back to quantized variant or hosted pool; also set a max latency threshold for fallback.
[12:33] Maya: What's the uplift to latency when falling back to hosted? We are sensitive to p95.
[12:38] Priya: It varies; hosted can be slightly higher p95 for heavy batches due to multi-tenant scheduling. We'll capture sample numbers in the sandbox run.
[12:48] [20-minute mark summary and a quick break]
[21:12] Priya: Back to the Console, here's a demo of the report builder. You can export weekly chargeback reports and schedule them to go to finance.
[21:25] Priya: I'll create a one-page 'route economics' snapshot: top 5 spenders, top cost drivers, and recommended actions (cache, quantize, move to Dedicated).
[21:38] Maya: That would be great. Can that report include predicted monthly cost if current trends continue?
[21:44] Priya: Yes we have a forecast model that projects cost based on recent rolling average with seasonality correction; it's not perfect but useful for planning.
[21:57] Samir: About forecasting — can we set hard alerts if forecasted spend exceeds X% of budget?
[22:03] Liam: Yep, set thresholds on the forecast and get alerts. You can also simulate 'what-if' by toggling model types or applying batching improvements to see projected savings.
[22:17] Jordan: Any first-party integrations for our observability stack? We use Datadog and Splunk.
[22:22] Alex: We have Datadog and Prometheus exporters; logs can be forwarded to Splunk. Also tracing hooks for distributed traces.
[22:32] Maya: Pricing ask — can you provide per-route and per-model unit price examples for both hosted and Dedicated?
[22:39] Alex: Yes we'll send a spreadsheet with per-token models and an example Dedicated commit with estimated monthly price per route. We'll include sample scenarios: steady-state, bursty, and mixed.
[22:53] Avery: If we want to run a pilot, what's the typical timeline?
[22:57] Priya: For a route-level pilot with sandboxes and perf run, 2-3 weeks to collect meaningful data; Dedicated proof can be longer depending on contract.
[23:06] Maya: And the billing for pilot? Trial credit or evaluation pricing?
[23:10] Alex: We can provide initial credits and a short-term evaluation rate for the sandbox run. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[23:21] [30-minute mark: deep dive into embeddings cost]
[30:10] Priya: Looking at embeddings: model selection matters — smaller embedding models reduce cost but may degrade nearest-neighbor recall. Optimize suggests a moderate-size model with quantization for nightly batch indexing, and a higher-quality model for interactive queries.
[30:30] Maya: So split batch vs interactive. That makes sense.
[30:36] Samir: Could we run batch indexing on Dedicated overnight to save money and run interactive on hosted?
[30:41] Liam: Yup, scheduling jobs to Dedicated pools overnight is a common pattern.
[30:48] Jordan: Any special network egress charges if we pull results across regions?
[30:52] Alex: Egress is shown in the waterfall; cross-region traffic will add network costs. We'll help estimate that.
[31:02] Priya: Quick demo of an anomaly root cause: here's a spike in token length after a client change — Console links to request traces so you can see the changed prompt payload. Note: request payloads are redacted by default in hosted.
[31:18] Maya: Redaction is important.
[31:21] Alex: We'll include the security pack and highlight redaction and KMS options.
[31:31] [40-minute mark: Q&A and objections]
[40:10] Maya: One objection — our procurement is wary of vendor lock in and model portability. How do you support portability?
[40:18] Alex: Redwood supports multiple open models and you can export logs and prompts; we encourage using model-agnostic prompts and provide eval tooling so you can compare locally. For Dedicated we can provide an on-prem bundle if needed.
[40:34] Jordan: Another concern: if we commit Dedicated capacity and usage drops, how flexible are resize options?
[40:41] Alex: We offer quarterly review and resizing clauses; there are penalties for huge downsize but usually we can reconfigure pools or allow transferable credits. We'll lay out options.
[40:55] Samir: Technical nit — you mentioned prefix caching. Do you support dynamic cache invalidation?
[41:01] Priya: Yes, you can purge keys via API, and TTLs can be set per-route.
[41:08] Maya: Last thing — can we demo a scheduled report and the archive of previous months?
[41:13] Priya: Sure, creating the scheduled report now. You can pick cohorting (by tag, route, or team) and set weekly/monthly cadence. Old reports are stored for 12 months by default for hosted, longer for enterprise add-on.
[41:32] Alex: Ok we'll recap next steps.
[41:36] Alex: Recap: 1) Alex to send pricing spreadsheet and security packet; 2) Priya to run sandbox perf with sample traffic once AtlasHealth shares CSV; 3) Customer will provision sandbox access and traffic sample; 4) Follow-up meeting to review perf results and Dedicated sizing.
[41:57] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[42:01] Jordan: Thanks, looking forward to the sandbox.
[42:04] Alex: Thanks, we'll send invites for next sync.
[42:10] [call ends]

References/links mentioned:
- Security pack (link to be emailed)
- Pricing spreadsheet (will be attached in follow-up)
- Sandbox instructions doc (will be shared by Priya)
